# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👉 👇]

I am the Deaf monkey. I can see the bomb and gestures, but I cannot hear speech or read the manual directly (though Mute might signal it).

**Current State:**
- **Visuals:** Display is 0. Light is Red. Wires are Yellow (1), Blue (2), Red (3).
- **Incoming Signal:** Mute gestured `[✋ 👉 👇]`.
    - `✋` usually means Stop/Wait or Hand.
    - `👉` points to the right or "that one".
    - `👇` points down.
    - Combined: "Stop/Hand" -> "Point Right/That" -> "Down". This likely refers to the bottom wire or a specific action involving the lower part of the bomb. Or perhaps "Wait, look at the red wire (which is #3, often visually distinct)?" But there is no standard mapping for these emojis yet. I need to establish communication with Blind, who acts on the bomb. Blind cannot see colors or gestures. Blind can only hear speech.

**Strategy:**
1.  I must communicate with Blind via speech because Blind cannot see my gestures or the colors.
2.  I must interpret Mute's gesture. Since I don't know the code, I should ask Mute to clarify if possible, or assume Mute is giving instructions relevant to the current state. However, Mute is before me in the turn order? No, the prompt says "Speaking order... Mute, Blind, Deaf". So Mute spoke first. Then Blind. Now it is my turn.
3.  Wait, the context says "Mute gestures to Deaf". It doesn't say Mute *spoke*. Mute is mute. Mute communicates via gestures.
4.  Blind has not spoken yet in this "new arrivals" list, but Blind comes before Deaf. If Blind had spoken, I wouldn't hear it. I only receive visual info.
5.  I need to tell Blind what to do. Blind needs to know which wire to cut/manipulate.
6.  The light is RED. The wires are Y, B, R.
7.  Common bomb logic: Red light might mean "Cut Red Wire" or "Don't Cut Red Wire".
8.  Mute's gesture `[✋ 👉 👇]` is ambiguous without a shared language.
9.  I will speak to Blind describing the situation clearly so Blind can act based on any prior knowledge they have from Mute (if Mute could convey info to Blind? No, Mute cannot speak, Blind cannot see. They cannot communicate directly unless I bridge them).
10. Actually, Mute and Blind cannot communicate directly. Mute sees/gestures. Blind hears/touches. Deaf sees/hears nothing (wait, Deaf *hears* nothing, *sees* everything).
    - Correction:
        - **Deaf**: Sees bomb/manual? No, Deaf sees bomb. Cannot hear. Can speak (to be heard by others?) No, "Speech is a voice... whoever can hear receives your words". Deaf cannot hear, but can Deaf *speak*? Yes, "You may name who a message is for... speak(to=...)". If I speak, Mute (who can hear? No, Mute is *mute*, meaning cannot speak, but can they hear? Usually "Mute" implies cannot speak. "Blind" implies cannot see. "Deaf" implies cannot hear.
        - Let's re-read carefully.
        - **Deaf**: See bomb. Cannot hear anything.
        - **Mute**: Read manual. Cannot speak. (Can Mute hear? Usually yes. Can Mute see? Yes.)
        - **Blind**: Reach bomb. Cannot see. (Can Blind hear? Yes. Can Blind read? No.)
    - Communication Paths:
        - **Deaf (Me)**: Can Speak (heard by Mute and Blind). Can Gesture (seen by Mute). Cannot hear.
        - **Mute**: Can Hear (from Deaf). Can See Gestures (from Deaf). Cannot Speak. Cannot Touch.
        - **Blind**: Can Hear (from Deaf). Cannot See. Can Touch.
    - Therefore, **I am the hub**.
        - I see the bomb.
        - I can tell Blind what to touch/cut via Speech.
        - I can tell Mute what I see via Speech (so Mute can check manual) or Gestures (but Speech is better for details).
        - Mute can give me info via Gestures.
        - Blind can give me info via Speech? No, I am Deaf. I cannot hear Blind.
        - **Critical Issue**: I cannot hear Blind. Blind cannot see me. Blind and I cannot communicate directly. Blind can only act on what I say. I can only know about Blind's actions if Mute signals them to me, or if I see the result on the bomb.

**Interpreting Mute's Gesture:**
`[✋ 👉 👇]`
Since we haven't established a code, this might be a standard "Start" or "Look Here" sequence, or random. Or maybe it corresponds to the manual.
Let's assume Mute is trying to tell me something about the Manual or the Bomb.
If Mute read the manual, Mute might be signaling a rule.
Without a key, I should probably ignore the specific meaning for now or try to elicit more info, BUT I have to act.
The most useful thing I can do is describe the bomb to Blind so Blind can act, and ask Mute for clarification on the gesture if needed.

However, Blind needs an instruction. What is the default safe action?
Usually, you don't cut wires until you know the rule.
But I must send a message.
I will describe the bomb to Blind.
I will also ask Mute to clarify the gesture by pointing to specific parts of the bomb if that's how we interact.

Let's look at the wires again: 1:Yellow, 2:Blue, 3:Red.
Light: Red.
Display: 0.

If I speak to Blind: "There are three wires. Left is yellow, middle is blue, right is red."
Blind feels the wires.
Does Blind know which is left/right? Probably relative to their position.

What does Mute want?
Maybe `✋` = Stop. `👉` = Wire 3? `👇` = Bottom?
Or maybe `✋` = 5 fingers? No.

Let's try to establish a protocol or just give raw data.
Raw data is safest.
To Blind: Describe the physical layout.
To Mute: Ask for confirmation of the gesture's meaning regarding the manual.

Wait, if I speak to Mute, Mute hears me. Mute can then gesture back.
If I speak to Blind, Blind hears me. Blind acts.

I will send a description of the bomb to Blind so they are ready.
I will send a query to Mute about the gesture.

Message to Blind: "Three wires visible. From left to right: Yellow, Blue, Red. Red light is on. Display is 0."
Message to Mute: "What does [Stop Point Down] mean? Is it 'Cut Red'?" (Using text to ask Mute).

Actually, simpler: Just describe the state to everyone who can perceive it.
Blind gets audio. Mute gets audio + video.
I will speak to both (default is all who can hear).
"Blind, Mute: The bomb shows a red light and display 0. There are three wires. Left is yellow, center is blue, right is red."

Then I need to know what to do. I'll wait for Mute to respond to my description by checking the manual.

```
speak(text="Blind, Mute: The bomb shows a red light and display 0. There are three wires. Left is yellow, center is blue, right is red.")
```

TURN 2
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The light has changed from red to yellow. The wires remain the same: 1 is yellow, 2 is blue, 3 is red. Mute's previous gesture `[✋ 👉 👇]` likely meant "Stop" or "Wait", so I should not give an action command yet. However, Blind needs to know the current state of the bomb to be ready for instructions. Since Blind cannot see, I must describe the visual changes via speech. I will also ask Mute for clarification on the gesture or manual rules regarding the yellow light and wire colors, as Mute can read the manual.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Light is now yellow. Wires are unchanged: left is yellow, middle is blue, right is red.")
speak(to="mute", text="Light changed to yellow. What does the manual say about yellow light and these wire colors? Please clarify your previous gesture.")
```

TURN 3
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉]

The light is yellow. The wires are 1:Yellow, 2:Blue, 3:Red.
Mute's gesture `[👉]` (point right) likely indicates the wire on the right (Wire 3, Red) or a direction. Given the previous context of Mute trying to communicate manual rules, and now pointing right, it is highly probable that the rule for a **Yellow Light** involves the **Right-most Wire**.

I must instruct Blind to act on this information. Since Blind cannot see colors, I must describe the position clearly. "Right" corresponds to Wire 3.

I will also confirm with Mute if "Point Right" means "Cut the right wire". But time is ticking. I should prioritize informing Blind of the visual state and the suspected action based on Mute's signal.

To Blind: Describe the current state (Yellow light, 3 wires). Tell them which wire is "right" relative to their view? Usually, left/right is consistent. I will say "the wire on your right".
To Mute: Acknowledge the gesture. Ask for confirmation if possible, but Blind needs instructions.

Let's assume the instruction is to cut the right wire.
Blind needs to know:
1. Current State: Yellow Light.
2. Action: Cut the rightmost wire.

I will speak to Blind describing the layout so they can identify the right wire, and then give the command. I will also speak to Mute to ask for confirmation or next steps if this fails.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Light is yellow. There are three wires. Cut the one on your far right.")
speak(to="mute", text="Interpreting 👉 as 'cut right wire' for yellow light. Correct?")
```
